operational-example.copy: Use Tree View as a bounded component: Display one hierarchical set of nodes with expansion, selection, and keyboard semantics without owning file management, permissions, or admin processs.

scenario.title: Tree View
scenario.meta: Selection and expansion, not route current
rationale: Tree View displays one hierarchical set of nodes with tree, treeitem, aria-expanded, and aria-selected semantics.
Selection uses Flow action as a non-color-only inset indicator; expansion uses action text for disclosure state.
Checkbox trees, permission editors, drag and drop, bulk operations, and route ownership belong to patterns until Flow scopes them explicitly.

rows.label: Selected node
rows.value: Uses aria-selected plus Flow action inset/background, not route current.

rows.label: Expanded node
rows.value: Uses aria-expanded and disclosure icon/text treatment.

rows.label: Boundary
rows.value: Checkbox trees and editors are patterns, not Tree View variants.

items.rule: Owns the visible Tree View container and spacing.
Provides visible meaning and accessible name.
Separates selected node state from expanded disclosure state. Selected uses aria-selected plus a Flow action inset/background; expanded uses aria-expanded and disclosure icon state.
Keeps context short and local to the component.

accessibility.statePrecedence: disabled, selected, expanded, focus, hover, default
items: Expose current state through text or ARIA where applicable.
Keep keyboard focus visible and predictable.
Respect reduced motion for motion-bearing variants.
Escalate to a pattern when behavior exceeds one local component.

variants.copy: Tree View has one package-backed visual variant: standard hierarchical nodes. Density changes scale through Flow context. Checkbox trees, permission editors, drag and drop, and bulk operations belong to patterns until scoped explicitly.

states.copy: Tree View states separate selection from disclosure: selected uses aria-selected with a Flow action inset/background, expanded uses aria-expanded and disclosure icon state, and focus/hover remain local interaction feedback.

variant-state-behavior.copy: Tree View keeps one visual variant. State controls selected, expanded, focus, hover, and disabled behavior; density controls scale. Tree-based editors and checkbox selection belong to patterns.

full-width.copy: Tree View may fill its parent when content remains readable and behavior stays local.

responsive-layout-patterns.copy: Use responsive density to preserve labels, state, and targets; do not add pattern orchestration to Tree View.

viewport-organization.copy: Viewport rules decide density and placement while Tree View remains a component.

items.title: Phone
items.rule: Use readable labels and touch-safe targets.

items.title: Tablet
items.rule: Keep the component near related context.

items.title: Desktop
items.rule: Use compact density only when state remains visible.

playground.copy: Use the playground to verify Tree View label, variant, state, full-width behavior, and pattern boundary.

api-foundations.copy: Tree View API exposes local props while Design System owns foundations, primitives, state precedence, and escalation rules.

props.name: onSelect
props.notes: Called when a node is selected.

props.name: density
props.notes: Tree row density: sm, md, or lg.

groups.title: Use
items: Use Tree View for one bounded component job.
Keep label, state, and context visible.
Use Design System tokens and accessibility rules.

groups.title: Avoid
items: Do not document checkbox tree as a Tree View variant until Flow scopes it.
Tree-based editors, permission configuration, drag and drop, and bulk operations belong to patterns.
Do not hide required meaning in icons, color, or animation only.
Do not add process orchestration inside the component.

groups.title: Review
items: Check role tree and treeitem semantics.
Check aria-selected and aria-expanded remain distinct.
Check pattern escalation for checkbox trees, editors, drag and drop, and bulk operations.

rejectIf: Checkbox tree is presented as a closed component variant without Flow scope decision.
Tree-based editors, permission configuration, drag and drop, and bulk operations belong to patterns.
Required label or fallback is missing.

miel.copy: MIEL treats Tree View as a bounded component. Agents may place it when the job is local; humans confirm state, accessibility, content, and whether escalation to a pattern is required.
canDecide: Use Tree View for one local UI job.
Select variant and state from the Tree View contract.
Keep labels, focus, and state visible.
mustAsk: The request needs orchestration, multi-step behavior, or cross-surface state.
Tree-based editors, permission configuration, drag and drop, and bulk operations belong to patterns.
Accessibility, risk, or reduced-motion expectations are unclear.
rejectIf: Tree-based editors, permission configuration, drag and drop, and bulk operations belong to patterns.
Required meaning is icon-only, color-only, or motion-only.
The component becomes a process container.
miel.handoff: I am using Tree View as a bounded component. Please confirm label, state, accessibility behavior, responsive treatment, and whether this should escalate to a pattern.
